does_not_establish: wall clock time on any physical part
memory system behaviour: flash wait states, bus contention, buffering
anything about a chip other than the one the TRM table describes
establishes: the compiled Q15 step executes the instruction mix the analytic model assumes, or differs from it in a way this document names
whether dyadic coefficients compile to shifts and adds rather than to multiplies or library calls
relative ordering and ratios between methods under the TRM table
that the C agrees with the pinned Python evaluator bit for bit, including where the Q15 primitives raise
accuracy.statement: The emulator is instruction accurate and NOT cycle accurate. It reports which instructions execute and in what order. Every cycle count here comes from applying the Cortex-M0+ TRM table to that instruction stream offline, under the assumptions below. No number here was measured on any physical part.

assumptions.multi_register_cycles: 1 + N for N registers, plus 2 more when the register list contains PC, which is the same pipeline refill that makes a taken branch cost 3

mnemonic_class.note: The five classes the cost model prices are taken from it unchanged, so load, store, mul, shift and add cost the same on both sides. The extension covers mnemonics a compiler emits that the pinned ten-line fixture does not contain; alu is one cycle, branch and multi-register transfers follow the assumptions block.

schema.crosscheck: agreement with the pinned Python evaluator: exact final int16 state, every stage input, and the operation index at which an overflow trapped
schema.cycles_analytic: costmodel.cycle_count for this tableau at n_states = 1, unchanged
schema.cycles_traced: TRM-priced cycles for every instruction executed inside rk_step in one step, excluding the derivative routine's own body
schema.cycles_traced_model_scope: the same pricing restricted to the instructions the analytic model prices: the load, the coefficient terms, the adds and the store
schema.instructions_by_region: executed instructions per step by what the source line does: load, coeff, store are the model's scope; hscale is the h times k product the model excludes; rhs_call is the call to the derivative; loop is loop control; frame is the stack frame
schema.muls_in_model_scope: of those, the ones applying a tableau coefficient
schema.muls_per_step: MULS instructions executed per step inside rk_step
schema.opcode_histogram: executed mnemonics per step inside rk_step
schema.state_scaling: the same counts at each state count the scored problem set uses, one through four, so the model's linear scaling in state dimension can be read rather than assumed. cycles_per_step is the whole rk_step at that state count, on the same scope as cycles_traced and so excluding the derivative routine's own body; cycles_analytic beside it is costmodel.cycle_count at the same state count

toolchain.debug_flag_note: -g adds a line table and no instructions; the region attribution reads it
toolchain.linker_script: text, data and bss placed contiguously from 0x0; a flat image

verdicts.crosscheck: 144 of 144 comparable cases agree with the pinned Python evaluator on the exact final int16 state and on every stage input. 25 of them are cases where the Q15 primitives raise, and on those the checked C traps at the same operation index. The reference C from emit_c keeps int32 intermediates and truncates at the store, so it returns a value instead of trapping; that is why a checked entry point exists and why the comparison reads the overflow verdict and not only the state.

inversions.note: the analytic model puts rk4 below rk38 and the trace puts rk38 below the other

verdicts.ordering: Spearman rank correlation between the analytic and the traced cycles per step across 9 methods is 0.9833 under m0plus_fast. 1 pair(s) rank differently: rk4 against rk38, analytic 33 and 36, traced 139 and 130.
verdicts.scope: The analytic model prices the stage and b combinations only. It prices no derivative call, no h times k product, no loop control and no stack frame, so the whole-step traced number is larger by construction. Both are published: ratio is whole step, ratio_model_scope is the matched scope.
